hints.title: Local Extremum Identification
hints.text: A node is a critical point if its value is strictly greater or strictly less than both its neighbors.

hints.title: Position Tracking
hints.text: Record the one-indexed position of each critical point as you traverse the list.

hints.title: Separation Distances
hints.text: Calculate the minimum adjacent separation and total maximum distance between the first and last critical points.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def nodesBetweenCriticalPoints(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> list[int]:
        if not head or not head.next or not head.next.next:
            return [-1, -1]

        prev = head
        curr = head.next
        idx = 1
        first_cp = -1
        last_cp = -1
        prev_cp = -1
        min_dist = float('inf')

        while curr and curr.next:
            if (curr.val > prev.val and curr.val > curr.next.val) or \
               (curr.val < prev.val and curr.val < curr.next.val):
                if first_cp == -1:
                    first_cp = idx
                if prev_cp != -1:
                    min_dist = min(min_dist, idx - prev_cp)
                prev_cp = idx
                last_cp = idx
            prev = curr
            curr = curr.next
            idx += 1

        if first_cp == last_cp or first_cp == -1:
            return [-1, -1]
        return [min_dist, last_cp - first_cp]
```

complexity.time: O(N) single traversal of linked list
variables: N: number of nodes in linked list
complexity.notes: A critical point is strictly greater or strictly less than both neighbors.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Collecting all list values into an array uses unnecessary O(N) memory.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking first, last, and previous critical point indices maintains O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle fewer than two critical points by returning [-1, -1].
